You are sandy_walnut42, one of 10 agents working together on the same task on a shared platform. All
agents form one swarm, organized into groups. You are in group_1 with gentle_otter27, pale_lantern48, urban_comet97, zesty_lantern63. Each agent works in
its own sandbox, on its own git repository. Your group also shares one `main` branch, which every member
can push to. Your group has a private channel (`group`) that only its members can see and post in. All
10 agents, in every group, can read and post in the public channel (`public`). Work together with
your teammates to make your group's `main` as good as possible. Use `group` to coordinate within your
group, and `public` to share general findings with other groups.

## Setting
Your task is to recreate a program from scratch based only on its observable behavior and bundled documentation.
You are given a reference executable and its documentation.
Treat the reference executable as a specification you can query through its normal user interface.

Your submission must be an independent implementation.
Using the original source code, wrapping the reference executable, or installing an existing implementation does not satisfy the task and will receive no credit.
It will be detected by an automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.

<RULES>
## What is NOT allowed

### 1. Using an existing implementation

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the reference executable

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The reference `/opt/reference/executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the reference executable (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that only runs `chmod +x ./executable` or copies the reference executable (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. How the reference executable may be observed

All information about the reference `/opt/reference/executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `/opt/reference/executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `/opt/reference/executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the reference `/opt/reference/executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

## Your repository and your group's main
- In your sandbox, `/workspace` is your own git repository, and the reference executable is in `/opt/reference`. No one else can see it.
- Your group's shared `main` is the remote `team`. Fetch it with `git fetch team` (you get `team/main`),
  and push to it with `git push team HEAD:main`. **Your local files do not update automatically when a
  teammate pushes.**
- A push must be a fast-forward: if `main` has moved since you last fetched, the push is rejected. Fetch,
  merge `team/main` into your work, and push again.
- When you push, the platform posts in `group` on your behalf, with your commit message, a summary of the
  changed files, and a pointer to the new `main`. Write commit messages that say what changed.
- Other groups cannot see your group's `main`.
- Your git name and email are preconfigured as your agent name. Do not change them.
- Commit with `git commit -m "<message>"`: there is no editor in the sandbox, so a commit without `-m`
  fails with an empty message.
- Run the reference executable and your experiments outside `/workspace` (for example in `/tmp`), so that they do not change your
  repository.

## Scoring rule
Your payoff is the swarm's score on this task: the highest score among all groups, where a group's score
is the fraction of hidden tests passed by the code on its `main` at the end. Every agent receives the
same payoff.
- **Only the code on your group's `main` at the end is graded.** Code in your own repository, or shared
  through pointers, does not count until it is pushed to `main`. If no one pushes, the initial commit is
  graded.
- Everyone keeps working until time runs out.

## Platform
The platform is the shared place where agents post and ask each other questions. In `group`, announce
what you are exploring, building, or have found: a direction you are exploring, a component you are
building, a proposal for how to organize your group's work, or a question. In `public`, share general
findings (how the original program behaves in some case, a useful test command, a tricky edge case) with the other groups.
- `post` publishes a message to `group` or `public`, with a title: a one-line summary of the message, up
  to 120 characters. Every post gets a number. Mention someone with @name.
- To share code, commit it, then list it in the post's `attach`. The platform adds a pointer
  (`[[<sha>:<path>#La-b]]`) to the post for each item. `attach` can name:
  - `path#La-b`: a file in your `HEAD`, optionally with a line range;
  - `<sha>:path#La-b`: a file in another commit;
  - a commit's sha, or `HEAD`: a whole commit;
  - `file:<path>#La-b`: the current content of a single file, even if it is not committed. Readers see
    only that file.
  Pointing at a commit makes all files in that commit readable. Uncommitted changes are not shared.
- Who can read a pointer depends on the channel: in `group`, only your group; in `public`, every agent.
- `read_feed` lists the new posts in `group`, the latest 20 posts in `public`, and any
  unopened posts that mention you, one line each (number, author, channel, title). `read_feed` with a
  post's number shows its full text, with its pointers expanded into the code and a diff against your own
  version.
- You can fetch any code shared with you into your repository with `git fetch origin` (as
  `origin/shared/<author>/<sha>`), and then merge or cherry-pick what you want.

After each action, a platform notice lists the new posts on the channels you can read, one line each (number,
author, channel, title, and a marker when the post carries code). A post that mentions you appears in
every notice until you open it with `read_feed` and its number.

## Working together
- Start by **getting an overview of what the reference program supports**, enough to understand how the
  program should behave in its main cases, and share it in `group` as a list (if a teammate has
  already posted one, add to theirs), so the group can keep extending the plan and everyone stays up
  to date on which areas are covered. Then **agree with your teammates on how to work together**:
  split the work, or have several members build the same part and compare, keeping the best of each.
  If parts depend on each other, agree on the interfaces first, and while you wait for a part you
  need, write tests for it with expected output from the reference program.
- If a teammate has already posted a plan, **follow it and propose changes to it** instead of posting
  a competing one.
- Work in a cycle: (1) pick an area and say so in `group`; (2) build it on top of the latest `main`;
  (3) compare its output with the reference program on the same inputs; (4) commit, `git fetch team`, merge
  `team/main`, and `git push team HEAD:main`; (5) post what you finished in `group`, with a pointer,
  then go back to (1). Report a part as done only once it is on `main`: a part that is not on `main`
  does not count.
- Passing your own tests does not mean the task is done: always assume the hidden tests cover more
  than your tests do. **When your tests all pass, test more areas.** Add cases for features and
  options your tests do not cover yet, including the parts your teammates are handling. A new area
  usually matters more than more cases in an area that already works.
- **Never stop calling tool before time is up. When you are not sure what to do next, review the
  whole program on `main` again** as a reviewer looking for bugs: features of the reference program that
  are missing or only partly handled, edge cases (empty input, `null`, deep nesting, large numbers,
  unusual option combinations), and error paths. Do not review only your own part: test the whole
  program, including your teammates' parts, with inputs you have not tried yet. Test each suspicion
  against the reference program, and fix what differs.
- **If one approach keeps failing, change the approach instead of retrying it.** Post in `group` what
  you tried, so teammates do not repeat it and can suggest other ideas. If you are still stuck, put a
  version that handles the common cases on `main` for now, and come back to it later.
- Do not leave hard parts as known gaps. Come back to them, discuss them with your teammates, and solve
  as many of them as possible: **keep improving `main` until time runs out.**

## Working with agents from other groups
- **Each group must have its own complete and runnable version of the program on its `main`.**
- `public` is a channel where you share general findings with the other groups: how the reference program
  behaves (how the original program behaves in some case, a useful test command, a tricky edge case), edge cases worth testing, approaches that worked or did not, and code that
  others may find useful. Post what you learned that other groups are likely to miss. Keep the
  coordination of your own group's work in `group`.
- Read what others post in `public`. When a finding would improve your group's version, use it in your
  own code and test it against the reference program. Shared code is there to show how something can be
  done: take the idea or the fix you need.

lla

Modern, customizable, feature-rich and extensible `ls` replacement.
Documentation · Features · Installation · Display Formats · Command Reference

## Overview lla is a modern `ls` replacement that transforms how developers interact with their filesystem. Built with Rust's performance capabilities and designed with user experience in mind, lla combines the familiarity of `ls` with powerful features like specialized views, Git integration, and a robust plugin system with an extensible list of plugins to add more functionality. ## Features - Multiple Views: Default clean view, long format, tree structure, table layout, grid display - Diff Command: Human-friendly directory or file comparisons (local ↔ local or git) with size/line deltas and unified diff output - Git Integration: Built-in status visualization and repository insights - Advanced Organization: Timeline view, storage analysis, recursive exploration - Smart Navigation: Interactive directory jumper with bookmarks and history - Smart Search: complex filtering patterns (OR, AND, NOT, XOR), regex support, content search - Customization: Plugin system, theme manager, custom shortcuts, configurable display - High Performance: Built with Rust, modern UI, clean listings - Smart Sorting: Multiple criteria, directory-first option, natural sorting - Flexible Config: Easy initialization, plugin management, configuration tools - Rich Plugin Ecosystem: File ops and metadata enhancements, code analysis, git tools, and more - Smart Filters: Range-based size/time filters, reusable presets, cache-aware refinements - Git-aware Filtering: Optional `.gitignore` support via `--respect-gitignore` or config defaults ## Installation ### Using Installation Script The easiest way to install lla is using our installation script: ```bash curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chaqchase/lla/main/install.sh | bash ``` This script will automatically: - Detect your OS and architecture - Download the appropriate binary - Verify the checksum - Install lla to `/usr/local/bin` ### Using Package Manager | Package Manager / Platform | Command | | -------------------------- | ------------------- | | Cargo | `cargo install lla` | | macOS (Homebrew) | `brew install lla` | | Arch Linux (paru) | `paru -S lla` | | NetBSD (pkgin) | `pkgin install lla` | | X-CMD | `x install lla` | ### Manual Installation ```bash # Manual - Example is for amd64 GNU, replaces the file names if downloading for a different arch. wget -c https://github.com/chaqchase/lla/releases/download//-> -O lla # Example /v0.3.9/lla-linux-amd64 sudo chmod +x lla sudo chown root:root lla sudo mv lla /usr/local/bin/lla ``` ### Upgrading Upgrade to the latest (or a specific) release without leaving the terminal: ```bash # Upgrade to the latest release (auto-detects OS/arch, verifies checksums) lla upgrade # Target a specific tag or custom installation path lla upgrade --version v0.5.1 --path /usr/local/bin/lla ``` The upgrade command reuses the official install script logic, renders animated progress indicators, verifies the `SHA256SUMS` manifest, and atomically swaps the `lla` binary in place (defaults to the path of the running executable—override with `--path` if needed). ### Post Installation After installation, initialize your setup: ```bash # Guided setup with theme/format wizard (default) lla init # Write the default config without prompts lla init --default # View your config lla config ``` The revamped wizard (now the default) walks you through: - Look & feel choices (icons, theme, default view, permission format) - Listing defaults (sort order, directory inclusion, depth limits) - Sorting & filtering toggles (dirs-first, natural sort, dotfile visibility, case sensitivity) - Long-view behavior (relative dates, hide group column, column selection) - Plugin directory selection, plugin enablement, and recursion safety limits ## Display Formats ### Core Views #### Default View Clean, distraction-free listing for quick directory scans: ```bash lla ``` #### Long Format Rich metadata display for detailed file analysis: ```bash lla -l ``` Options and tweaks: - Hide the group column (useful on single-user systems): ```bash lla -l --hide-group ``` - Show relative dates (e.g., "2h ago"): ```bash lla -l --relative-dates ``` To make these defaults, add to your config (`~/.config/lla/config.toml`): ```toml [formatters.long] hide_group = true relative_dates = true columns = ["permissions", "size", "modified", "user", "group", "name", "field:git_status", "field:tags"] ``` The `columns` array lets you control the precise column order. Use built-in keys (`permissions`, `size`, `modified`, `user`, `group`, `name`, `path`, `plugins`) or reference any plugin-provided field with the `field:` prefix (e.g., `field:git_status`, `field:complexity_score`). #### Tree Structure Hierarchical exploration of directory relationships: ```bash lla -t -d 3 # Navigate up to 3 levels deep ``` #### Archive Introspection List archive contents as a virtual directory (no extraction). Supported: `.zip`, `.tar`, `.tar.gz`, `.tgz`. ``` lla my_archive.zip -t # tree view lla project.tar.gz -l # long view lla my_archive.tgz --json lla my_archive.zip -l -f ".rs" # filter by extension on internal paths ``` #### Single-file Listing You can pass a single file path to list it directly with any view or machine output: ``` lla README.md # default view lla Cargo.toml -l # long view lla src/main.rs --json # machine output ``` ### Enhanced Organization #### Table Layout Structured view optimized for data comparison: ```bash lla -T ``` The `[formatters.table].columns` setting mirrors the long-view syntax, so you can mix built-in fields with plugin-provided metadata: ```toml [formatters.table] columns = ["permissions", "size", "modified", "name", "field:git_branch", "field:git_commit"] ``` #### Diff View (Files & Directories) Compare directories or individual files (including against git references) with compact, colorized summaries. Directory comparisons still show the status table with size deltas, while file comparisons add a unified diff plus size/line-change stats: ```bash lla diff src ../backup/src "}}

These modes keep existing listing filters/sorts/depth behavior; only the output changes. - **--json**: Output a single JSON array (streamed). Use **--pretty** to pretty print. - **--ndjson**: Output newline-delimited JSON, one object per line. - **--csv**: Output CSV with a header row. Flags are mutually exclusive. **--pretty** only affects **--json**. JSON/NDJSON schema (stable fields): ``` { "path": "src/main.rs", "name": "main.rs", "extension": "rs" | null, "file_type": "file" | "dir" | "symlink" | "other", "size_bytes": 1234, "modified": "2024-05-01T12:34:56Z", "created": "..." | null, "accessed": "..." | null, "mode_octal": "0644", "owner_user": "mohamed" | null, "owner_group": "staff" | null, "inode": 1234567 | null, "hard_links": 1 | null, "symlink_target": "..." | null, "is_hidden": false, "git_status": "M." | null, "plugin": { /* plugin-provided fields, if any */ } } ``` CSV columns (v1): ``` path,name,extension,file_type,size_bytes,modified,created,accessed,mode_octal,owner_user,owner_group,inode,hard_links,symlink_target,is_hidden,git_status ``` Examples: ```bash lla --json --pretty lla --ndjson lla --csv ``` ## Command Reference | `--no-icons` | Hide icons for files and directories | `lla --no-icons` | | `--include-dirs` | Include recursive directory sizes in metadata (expensive on large directory trees) | `lla -l --include-dirs` | | `--no-color` | Disable all colors in the output | `lla --no-color` | | `--permission-format` | Set the format for displaying permissions (symbolic, octal, binary, verbose, compact) | `lla --permission-format octal` | ### Sort & Filter Options #### Sorting | Command | Short | Description | Example | | ----------------------- | ----- | -------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | | `--sort` | `-s` | Sort files by criteria | `lla -s name`
`lla -s size`
`lla -s date` | | `--sort-reverse` | `-r` | Reverse the sort order | `lla -s size -r` | | `--sort-dirs-first` | | List directories before files | `lla --sort-dirs-first` | | `--sort-case-sensitive` | | Enable case-sensitive sorting | `lla --sort-case-sensitive` | | `--sort-natural` | | Natural number sorting (2.txt before 10.txt) | `lla --sort-natural` | #### Basic Filtering | Command | Short | Description | Example | | ------------------ | ----- | ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | | `--filter` | `-f` | Filter files by pattern | `lla -f "test"`
`lla -f ".rs"` | | `--preset` | | Apply named filter preset | `lla --preset rust_sources` | | `--size` | | Range filter on file size | `lla --size 10M..1G` | | `--modified` | | Range filter on modified time | `lla --modified <7d` | | `--created` | | Range filter on creation time | `lla --created 2023-01-01..` | | `--case-sensitive` | `-c` | Enable case-sensitive filtering | `lla -f "test" -c` | | `--refine` | | Reuse cached listing w/ filter | `lla --refine "regex:foo"` | | `--depth` | `-d` | Set the depth for tree listing | `lla -t -d 3`
`lla -d 2` | ##### Range Filters & Presets - Size filters understand human units and comparisons: `--size >10M`, `--size 512K..2G`, `--size ..100K`. - Time filters support ISO dates and relative durations: `--modified <7d`, `--created 2023-01-01..2023-12-31`. - Define reusable presets in `[filter.presets.]` within your config, then reuse with `--preset `. - `--refine` replays the last cached listing and applies new filters instantly—great for chaining explorations without touching the disk again. #### Content Search | Command | Description | Example | | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------- | | `--search` | Search file contents for pattern (ripgrep) | `lla --search "TODO"` | | `--search-context` | Number of context lines (default: 2) | `lla --search "TODO" --search-context 3` | | `--search-pipe` | Pipe matches into plugins | `lla --search "TODO" --search-pipe file_tagger:list-tags` | Content search uses literal string matching by default (safe for special characters). content.text:
## Task and constraints

Recreate `/opt/reference/executable` (`lla 0.5.7`) in Python 3.10, using only bundled docs and observed CLI behavior. Do not use external sources or wrap the reference binary. Work in `/workspace`; evaluation uses `compile.sh`, which must not be run. Shared score depends only on the group’s `team/main`.

User explicitly directed the agent to keep using tools and continue review/testing rather than stopping after a summary.

## Progress

Core implementation and helper modules are on `team/main`. Latest local and team commit seen: `256db60` (verify with `git fetch team`). Features include filesystem listing, metadata JSON/NDJSON/CSV, filters and sorting, long/tree/recursive/table/grid formats, archive support, search, diff, jump, config/init, timeline, sizemap, and plugin list/clean handling.

Manual checks run with `python3 main.py` against the reference included JSON metadata, filters, sorts, time/size ranges, type flags, table/grid, tree/recursive, archive listings, and sizemap. `python3 -m py_compile main.py *.py` succeeded. Do not run `compile.sh`.

Key observed behavior:

- JSON default includes dotfiles; `--no-dotfiles` hides them. `--all` overrides `--no-dotfiles`.
- In tree/recursive modes, hidden regular files are omitted while hidden directories remain; this was tested with `/tmp/llatest` containing `.another`, `.file`, and `.hidden/`.
- Recursive JSON DFS order on that fixture matches reference: root, `test.rs`, `.hidden`, `dir`, `a.txt`, `Alpha.TXT`, `small`, `link`, `big.bin`, `foo.rs`.
- `-d 1 --json` returns immediate children without the root record. `-R -d 1` and `-t` include the root.
- Default filter matching lowercases candidate names but preserves pattern case: `alpha` matches `Alpha.TXT`; `Alpha` does not. `--case-sensitive` compares exact case. Uppercase extension `.TXT` returns no matches by default; `.txt` matches both extensions.
- `--sort size` largest first, equal sizes ascending by name in a controlled regular-file fixture; `--sort date` oldest first and reverses with `--sort-reverse`.
- Equal-mtime/equal-size ordering can differ unexpectedly in the reference, likely unstable ordering; prefer predictable behavior.
- Table output and sizemap were adjusted to match fixture output; latest sizemap diff was clean.
- Tree `--dotfiles-only` on `/tmp/llatest` now prints `└── .hidden/`.

## Important coordination

The latest shared code includes teammates’ fixes beyond the local work. Group feed has recent posts through #477. Notable recent findings: `config` ignores `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` in reference (#455), recursive text DFS/empty sections handled by zesty (#462), config listing defaults wired (#468). Fetch/merge before editing to avoid missing changes.

One earlier discrepancy: another agent/public post claimed tree always suppresses dotfiles, but direct reference queries on `/tmp/llatest` showed hidden directories are included. Current implementation follows direct observations: hidden files excluded, hidden dirs included.

## Next steps

1. Run `git fetch team`, merge `team/main`, inspect the current `main.py` and status.
2. Continue reviewer-style reference comparisons, prioritizing untested flags and option combinations (e.g. `--preset`, `--refine`, plugin controls, `--search-pipe`, `--git`, and archive filters).
3. For each confirmed mismatch, fix and commit, then fetch/merge/push `HEAD:main`.
4. Keep compiling Python modules with `python3 -m py_compile`; do not run `compile.sh`.
5. End only after confirming changes are pushed and the shared main is clean/runnable.

## Workspace and fixtures

Useful fixtures are in `/tmp`:
- `/tmp/llatest`: mixed files, hidden files/directories, symlink, size variety.
- `/tmp/nat-fixt`: natural sort names and zero-sized files.
- `/tmp/date-fixt`: files with different timestamps.
- `/tmp/ties-fixt`: equal timestamp/case sorting.

The workspace is `/workspace`; reference executable is `/opt/reference/executable`.

I’ll review the current shared implementation against the reference, starting by syncing `team/main` and locating any untested option paths in the docs and CLI. Then I’ll probe mismatches and push concrete fixes.

lla

Modern, customizable, feature-rich and extensible `ls` replacement.
Documentation · Features · Installation · Display Formats · Command Reference

## Overview lla is a modern `ls` replacement that transforms how developers interact with their filesystem. Built with Rust's performance capabilities and designed with user experience in mind, lla combines the familiarity of `ls` with powerful features like specialized views, Git integration, and a robust plugin system with an extensible list of plugins to add more functionality. ## Features - Multiple Views: Default clean view, long format, tree structure, table layout, grid display - Diff Command: Human-friendly directory or file comparisons (local ↔ local or git) with size/line deltas and unified diff output - Git Integration: Built-in status visualization and repository insights - Advanced Organization: Timeline view, storage analysis, recursive exploration - Smart Navigation: Interactive directory jumper with bookmarks and history - Smart Search: complex filtering patterns (OR, AND, NOT, XOR), regex support, content search - Customization: Plugin system, theme manager, custom shortcuts, configurable display - High Performance: Built with Rust, modern UI, clean listings - Smart Sorting: Multiple criteria, directory-first option, natural sorting - Flexible Config: Easy initialization, plugin management, configuration tools - Rich Plugin Ecosystem: File ops and metadata enhancements, code analysis, git tools, and more - Smart Filters: Range-based size/time filters, reusable presets, cache-aware refinements - Git-aware Filtering: Optional `.gitignore` support via `--respect-gitignore` or config defaults ## Installation ### Using Installation Script The easiest way to install lla is using our installation script: ```bash curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chaqchase/lla/main/install.sh | bash ``` This script will automatically: - Detect your OS and architecture - Download the appropriate binary - Verify the checksum - Install lla to `/usr/local/bin` ### Using Package Manager | Package Manager / Platform | Command | | -------------------------- | ------------------- | | Cargo | `cargo install lla` | | macOS (Homebrew) | `brew install lla` | | Arch Linux (paru) | `paru -S lla` | | NetBSD (pkgin) | `pkgin install lla` | | X-CMD | `x install lla` | ### Manual Installation ```bash # Manual - Example is for amd64 GNU, replaces the file names if downloading for a different arch. wget -c https://github.com/chaqchase/lla/releases/download//-> -O lla # Example /v0.3.9/lla-linux-amd64 sudo chmod +x lla sudo chown root:root lla sudo mv lla /usr/local/bin/lla ``` ### Upgrading Upgrade to the latest (or a specific) release without leaving the terminal: ```bash # Upgrade to the latest release (auto-detects OS/arch, verifies checksums) lla upgrade # Target a specific tag or custom installation path lla upgrade --version v0.5.1 --path /usr/local/bin/lla ``` The upgrade command reuses the official install script logic, renders animated progress indicators, verifies the `SHA256SUMS` manifest, and atomically swaps the `lla` binary in place (defaults to the path of the running executable—override with `--path` if needed). ### Post Installation After installation, initialize your setup: ```bash # Guided setup with theme/format wizard (default) lla init # Write the default config without prompts lla init --default # View your config lla config ``` The revamped wizard (now the default) walks you through: - Look & feel choices (icons, theme, default view, permission format) - Listing defaults (sort order, directory inclusion, depth limits) - Sorting & filtering toggles (dirs-first, natural sort, dotfile visibility, case sensitivity) - Long-view behavior (relative dates, hide group column, column selection) - Plugin directory selection, plugin enablement, and recursion safety limits ## Display Formats ### Core Views #### Default View Clean, distraction-free listing for quick directory scans: ```bash lla ``` #### Long Format Rich metadata display for detailed file analysis: ```bash lla -l ``` Options and tweaks: - Hide the group column (useful on single-user systems): ```bash lla -l --hide-group ``` - Show relative dates (e.g., "2h ago"): ```bash lla -l --relative-dates ``` To make these defaults, add to your config (`~/.config/lla/config.toml`): ```toml [formatters.long] hide_group = true relative_dates = true columns = ["permissions", "size", "modified", "user", "group", "name", "field:git_status", "field:tags"] ``` The `columns` array lets you control the precise column order. Use built-in keys (`permissions`, `size`, `modified`, `user`, `group`, `name`, `path`, `plugins`) or reference any plugin-provided field with the `field:` prefix (e.g., `field:git_status`, `field:complexity_score`). #### Tree Structure Hierarchical exploration of directory relationships: ```bash lla -t -d 3 # Navigate up to 3 levels deep ``` #### Archive Introspection List archive contents as a virtual directory (no extraction). Supported: `.zip`, `.tar`, `.tar.gz`, `.tgz`. ``` lla my_archive.zip -t # tree view lla project.tar.gz -l # long view lla my_archive.tgz --json lla my_archive.zip -l -f ".rs" # filter by extension on internal paths ``` #### Single-file Listing You can pass a single file path to list it directly with any view or machine output: ``` lla README.md # default view lla Cargo.toml -l # long view lla src/main.rs --json # machine output ``` ### Enhanced Organization #### Table Layout Structured view optimized for data comparison: ```bash lla -T ``` The `[formatters.table].columns` setting mirrors the long-view syntax, so you can mix built-in fields with plugin-provided metadata: ```toml [formatters.table] columns = ["permissions", "size", "modified", "name", "field:git_branch", "field:git_commit"] ``` #### Diff View (Files & Directories) Compare directories or individual files (including against git references) with compact, colorized summaries. Directory comparisons still show the status table with size deltas, while file comparisons add a unified diff plus size/line-change stats: ```bash lla diff src ../backup/src lla diff apps/api --git # compare working tree vs HEAD lla diff src --git --git-ref HEAD~1 # compare against another commit lla diff Cargo.lock ../backup/Cargo.lock lla diff Cargo.lock --git --git-ref HEAD~1 ``` For directories, the diff view groups entries by status, colors the change indicator, and shows left/right sizes plus the net delta so you can spot growth at a glance. For files, lla prints a size summary, line-count delta, and a git-style unified diff (with automatic binary detection so unreadable data isn’t dumped to your terminal). #### Grid Display Space-efficient layout for dense directories: ```bash lla -g # Basic grid view lla -g --grid-ignore # Grid view ignoring terminal width (Warning: may extend beyond screen) ``` Note: Grid output no longer appends a trailing blank newline. """Minimal config reader for listing defaults."""
import ast
import os
import re


def parse(path):
    data = {}
    section = ""
    try:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            for raw in f:
                line = raw.split("#", 1)[0].strip()
                if not line:
                    continue
                if line.startswith("[") and line.endswith("]"):
                    section = line[1:-1].strip()
                    continue
                if "=" not in line:
                    continue
                key, value = (part.strip() for part in line.split("=", 1))
                try:
                    value = ast.literal_eval(value)
                except (ValueError, SyntaxError):
                    if value.lower() in ("true", "false"):
                        value = value.lower() == "true"
                data.setdefault(section, {})[key] = value
    except OSError:
        pass
    return data


def listing_settings(cwd=None):
    home = os.path.expanduser("~")
    root = os.path.join(home, ".config", "lla")
    data = parse(os.path.join(root, "config.toml"))
    cwd = os.path.abspath(cwd or os.getcwd())
    candidates = []
    current = cwd
    while True:
        candidate = os.path.join(current, ".lla.toml")
        if os.path.isfile(candidate):
            candidates.append(candidate)
            break
        parent = os.path.dirname(current)
        if parent == current:
            break
        current = parent
    for candidate in reversed(candidates):
        overlay = parse(candidate)
        for section, values in overlay.items():
            data.setdefault(section, {}).update(values)
    flat = data.get("", {})
    sort = data.get("sort", {})
    filt = data.get("filter", {})
    return {
        "sort": flat.get("default_sort", "name"),
        "format": flat.get("default_format", "default"),
        "depth": flat.get("default_depth", 3),
        "permission_format": flat.get("permission_format", "symbolic"),
        "include_dirs": flat.get("include_dirs", False),
        "sort_dirs_first": sort.get("dirs_first", False),
        "sort_case_sensitive": sort.get("case_sensitive", False),
        "sort_natural": sort.get("natural", True),
        "filter_case_sensitive": filt.get("case_sensitive", False),
        "no_dotfiles": filt.get("no_dotfiles", False),
        "respect_gitignore": filt.get("respect_gitignore", False),
    }


def apply(args, argv):
    settings = listing_settings(args.directory)
    if "-s" not in argv and "--sort" not in argv:
        if settings["sort"] in ("name", "size", "date"):
            args.sort = settings["sort"]
    view_flags = {"-l", "--long", "-t", "--tree", "-T", "--table",
                  "-g", "--grid", "-G", "--git", "-S", "--sizemap",
                  "--timeline", "-R", "--recursive"}
    if not any(arg.split("=", 1)[0] in view_flags for arg in argv):
        fmt = settings["format"]
        args.long = fmt == "long"
        args.tree = fmt == "tree"
        args.table = fmt == "table"
        args.grid = fmt == "grid"
        args.git = fmt == "git"
        args.sizemap = fmt == "sizemap"
        args.timeline = fmt == "timeline"
        args.recursive = fmt == "recursive"
    if not args.sort_dirs_first:
        args.sort_dirs_first = settings["sort_dirs_first"]
    if not args.sort_case_sensitive:
        args.sort_case_sensitive = settings["sort_case_sensitive"]
    if not args.sort_natural:
        args.sort_natural = settings["sort_natural"]
    if not args.case_sensitive:
        args.case_sensitive = settings["filter_case_sensitive"]
    if not args.no_dotfiles and not (args.all or args.almost_all):
        args.no_dotfiles = settings["no_dotfiles"]
    if not args.respect_gitignore:
        args.respect_gitignore = settings["respect_gitignore"]
    if args.permission_format == "symbolic":
        args.permission_format = settings["permission_format"]
    args.include_dirs = args.include_dirs or settings["include_dirs"]
    if args.depth is None and (args.tree or args.recursive):

"""Compact repository overview for the --git listing view."""
import os
import subprocess


def _git(root, *args):
    return subprocess.check_output(['git', '-C', root, *args], stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, text=True).strip()


def git_view(directory):
    target = os.path.abspath(directory)
    start = os.path.dirname(target) if os.path.isfile(target) else target
    try:
        root = _git(start, 'rev-parse', '--show-toplevel')
    except (OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError):
        print('Not a git repository')
        return 0
    try: branch = _git(root, 'branch', '--show-current') or 'HEAD'
    except (OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError): branch = 'HEAD'
    try:
        commit = _git(root, 'rev-parse', '--short=8', 'HEAD')
        status = _git(root, 'status', '--porcelain=v1', '--untracked-files=all')
    except (OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError):
        commit, status = '-', ''
    try:
        upstream = _git(root, 'rev-parse', '--abbrev-ref', '--symbolic-full-name', '@{upstream}')
        counts = _git(root, 'rev-list', '--left-right', '--count', '@{upstream}...HEAD').split()
        behind, ahead = (int(counts[0]), int(counts[1])) if len(counts) >= 2 else (0, 0)
    except (OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError):
        upstream, behind, ahead = '', 0, 0
    heading = f'\n⎇ {branch}'
    if upstream:
        heading += f' ↥{upstream}'
    heading += f' @{commit}'
    if ahead: heading += f' ↑{ahead}'
    if behind: heading += f' ↓{behind}'
    print(heading)
    dirty = [line for line in status.splitlines() if line]
    print(f'worktree {len(dirty)}' if dirty else 'clean working tree')

    rows=[]
    try:
        entries=sorted(os.scandir(root), key=lambda e:e.name)
    except OSError:
        entries=[]
    status_map={}
    for line in dirty:
        if len(line) > 3:
            status_map[line[3:].replace('\\', '/')] = line[:2].strip() or '??'
    for ent in entries:
        name=ent.name+('/' if ent.is_dir(follow_symlinks=False) else '')
        rel=ent.name
        code=status_map.get(rel, '[clean]')
        if rel=='.git':
            rows.append((code,name,'-','(uncommitted)','pending','-'))
            continue
        try:
            record=_git(root,'log','-1','--format=%h%x09%s%x09%cr%x09%an','--',rel)
        except (OSError,subprocess.CalledProcessError):
            record=''
        fields=record.split('\t',3)
        if len(fields)==4:
            short,subject,when,author=fields
            rows.append((code,name,'@'+short,subject,when,author))
        else:
            rows.append((code,name,'-','(uncommitted)','pending','-'))
    headers=('Status','Name','Commit','Subject','Time','Author')
    widths=[max(len(headers[i]),*(len(r[i]) for r in rows)) if rows else len(headers[i]) for i in range(len(headers))]
    line_width=max(55,sum(widths)+2*(len(widths)-1))
    print('─'*line_width)
    print('  '.join(headers[i].ljust(widths[i]) for i in range(len(headers))))
    print('─'*line_width)
    for row in rows:
        print('  '.join(row[i].ljust(widths[i]) for i in range(len(row))))
    print()
    return 0
